rules: The playfield owns the full viewport; status, feedback, reaction, and context regions overlap only quiet scenery or their world anchor as explicitly declared.
No UI may cover the courier, partner, Mira, bottle, movement corridor, route threshold, hazard tell, destination, or active interaction glyph.
Request and carried status remain at opposite upper corners and never compete for the fork or destination.
Lower feedback is temporary, limited to one or two short lines, and cannot become a persistent log.
Both route counterfactuals remain simultaneously visible until movement commits the courier to one physical path.
Follow-up destinations remain physical pennants selected by movement and context action, never cards or modal buttons.

roles.label: Pixel display identity
roles.purpose: Short route and place identity such as Gust, Shelter, Sunmill, and Herbalist.
roles.treatment: Expressive high-contrast pixel display face at 10 native pixels; never used for sustained reading.

roles.label: Readable gameplay copy
roles.purpose: Requests, reactions, instructions, and causal explanations.
roles.treatment: License-compatible humanist sans with strong hinting at 12 native pixels and 14-17 pixel line height.

roles.label: Potion values
roles.purpose: Warmth and soothing quantities and before/after comparisons.
roles.treatment: Semibold tabular numerals at 12 native pixels paired with angular sun and rounded leaf icons.

roles.label: World action cue
roles.purpose: One short context verb beside the active world object.
roles.treatment: Compact high-contrast 11 native pixel label plus a shipping-input glyph; clamp away from screen edges.

rules: No sustained reading is authored below 11 native pixels.
No feedback surface exceeds two short lines.
Text maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast against its authored surface.
Warmth and soothing always use icon, shape, word or number; hue is never the sole carrier.
The runtime must replace target-rendered lettering with licensed fonts while preserving these bounds and roles.

beats.label: Inhabited village continuity
beats.trigger: Scene is active between player actions.
beats.visibleResponse: Cauldron simmers when available, characters breathe with offset phases, and vane, pennants, and awning preview route conditions without synchronized decorative noise.

beats.label: Ingredient interaction response
beats.trigger: Courier uses the context action at Ember or Moss.
beats.visibleResponse: The proximity cue tightens, courier leans, the ingredient pops toward the cauldron, and the brew answers in the ingredient's shape language.

beats.label: Brew produces a persistent bottle
beats.trigger: The player commits the completed mix.
beats.visibleResponse: Cauldron compresses then flashes once, a bottle rises into the courier's hand, and the carried badge appears only after the physical bottle exists.

beats.label: Gust converts potion state
beats.trigger: Courier crosses the exposed route threshold by movement.
beats.visibleResponse: Vane and cloth anticipate the gust, courier braces, one soothing leaf exchanges into one warmth sun inside the visible bottle, then badge and lower strip confirm +1 warmth and -1 soothing.

beats.label: Shelter visibly preserves potion state
beats.trigger: Courier crosses the sheltered route threshold by movement.
beats.visibleResponse: Awning encloses the courier, a mint lock/check pulse appears behind the bottle, its marks remain locked, and the lower strip affirmatively confirms preservation.

beats.label: Exact-match reaction
beats.trigger: Courier hands the exposed-route potion to Mira.
beats.visibleResponse: Bottle handoff precedes Mira's open-armed relief and warm response; the comparison slip appears only after her physical reaction begins.

beats.label: Mismatch reaction and recovery
beats.trigger: Courier hands the sheltered-route potion to Mira.
beats.visibleResponse: Bottle handoff precedes a tucked-elbow shiver and distinct shake arc; comparison copy attributes the mismatch only after the pose reads.

beats.label: Reaction settles into the next embodied choice
beats.trigger: Mira's reaction settles and follow-up state becomes available.
beats.visibleResponse: The comparison slip withdraws, Sunmill and Herbalist pennants activate in world, and walking to Sunmill lights its route motif while dimming the alternative.

continuityRules: Courier, partner, Mira, bottle, buildings, route thresholds, and UI anchors retain identity, scale, and position across state transitions except for causal actor movement.
Ambient loops use varied phase and low contrast; no unrelated particles, permanent camera shake, synchronized motion, or animation quota.
Gameplay effects stage anticipation, impact, state change, confirmation, and settle without obscuring potion icons or traversal.
The fixed shipping camera never cuts during this delivery; the world remains the persistent context for every state.

findings: Proposed selection remains continuous-causal-village because both embodied route counterfactuals and the recipient remain attributable in one fixed view.
All eight selected views share one persistent world basis, admit only declared causal patches, and have exact native plus integer-3x review presentations.
Follow-up need tags flank protected geometry; the courier, both physical pennants, selection differentiation, E GO cue, and walking corridor remain simultaneously visible.
Every component separates tight per-state target placement from expected runtime frame size and uses a pivot that exactly matches its declared top-left, center, or bottom-center semantics.

Authoritative contract identity and all component lineage use the selected primary-view SHA-256; a separate complete-target fingerprint covers all required view hashes, prompt identities, experience rules, native geometry, and the component map.
All eight component overlays are rebuilt from declared viewport anchors and checked for exact placement reconstruction, clipping, protected-geometry intersections, and off-viewport bounds.
Generated scenes and native paintovers remain proposed whole-screen targets only; component.production is absent and no production asset claim is made.

metadata.generationTool: built-in image_gen references plus deterministic Pillow native-spec recomposition
metadata.hypothesis: A single world-first 480x270 village with compact edge UI can keep brewing, route choice, potion mutation, recipient reaction, and the next choice causally reconstructable without collapsing play into panels.
metadata.selectionReason: The selected direction keeps the brew yard, both physical route alternatives, the courier, and Mira simultaneously attributable. The closer comparison improves actor scale but the central building compresses the counterfactual-route read and makes the village feel more like connected pockets.

selectedViewReviews.finding: Measured request/carried surfaces leave both embodied route counterfactuals unobscured.
Both ingredient cues stay at the brew yard, and the detailed lower-right roof geometry is inherited unchanged from the persistent world basis.
Moss identity, a relocated unobscuring E ADD cue, cauldron response, and two-line causal feedback share one readable brew context.
World action remains primary; measured copy confirms the visible W1/S2 to W2/S1 change.
Positive preservation feedback is readable and does not substitute for the in-world lock/check response.
Relief pose precedes readable arrived-state and exact-match attribution.
Distinct shiver pose precedes readable mismatch attribution and preserves recovery.
The courier, both physical pennants, and the walking corridor remain visible; compact need tags flank protected geometry and E GO sits beside the courier.

normalization.repair: The generated sources now serve only as complete-scene composition references. Every selected state starts from one persistent 480x270 world basis, then admits only declared causal actor/effect patches and measured UI; 3x review files are exact nearest-neighbor presentations.

limitations: Deterministic engine captures prove causal execution, not human comprehension or fun.
These files are proposed whole-screen targets and native geometry specifications, not running Godot captures or production assets.
The generated village imagery remains a composition reference; downstream art must be reconstructed at native or declared integer scale after approval.
Segoe UI is used only to measure and demonstrate the humanist typography role in these target files; production integration must bundle a license-compatible matched font.
No isolated, extracted, engine-ready, or production component exists before scene-target approval.
